about: Test vectors for the ai-co2 statistics. Written by "node check.mjs --write" from estimate.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
howToCompare: Run everything in one process, in the order of this file. "node check.mjs --port your-module.mjs" does exactly what is listed here.
vectors: call estimate(input, options) and compare every number in `expected`.
A number passes when |got - expected| <= tolerance.relative × |expected| + tolerance.absolute. An expected 0 must be exactly 0.
true, false, null and text must match exactly. A "not a number" is not null. Lists must have the same length.
All masses are kg CO2e. `car` and `carExtreme` are km. Shares are fractions from 0 to 1. `pins` are track positions.
input.tips are stored as data: { id, whatIf, spec }. Build each tip as { id, change }: whatIf "moveShare" gives moveShare(spec), "scaleTokens" gives scaleTokens(spec).

whatIf "callsEstimate" wraps another what-if (spec.whatIf, spec.spec): before it answers, the tip calls estimate({ rows, hidden, tips: [{ id: "inner", change: inner }], applied: ["inner"], pins: { energy: 1 } }, { tips: false, biggestUnknown: false }) on the usage it was given, and then returns inner(usage).

whatIf "broken" is a tip that breaks one rule on purpose. spec.how says which: "edits-its-input" sets usage.rows[0].output = 0 and returns the usage; "returns-nothing" returns undefined; "is-async" is an async function; "rows-not-a-list" returns { rows: null, hidden }; "forgets-hidden" returns { rows }; "drops-a-piece" returns the hidden list without its first piece; "reorders-pieces" returns the hidden list reversed; "changes-a-slot" gives the first piece slot 5; "changes-an-amount" gives the first piece the amount [0.5, 1, 8]; "negative-count" gives every row output -1; "no-function" has text in place of the function.
In stored inputs and options the texts "@NaN", "@Infinity" and "@-Infinity" stand for those three numbers, which JSON cannot hold.
mustThrow: building the tips or calling estimate(input, options) must throw an error whose message contains every text in `says`.
scenarios: scenarioOfDot(input, dot) must give `expected`. `run` is a whole number and must match exactly.

carry: carryThrough(spread, rule, dots) with rule(kg) = perKg × kg, or perKgFrom × kg from `from` kg up when the rule has those two, and at least `minimum` when the rule has one. Leave `dots` out when it is null. It must give `expected`, or throw when `refused` is true.
scale: fitScale(top) must give scaleMax for every entry of scale.fit. nextScale(previous, range, baseline, dragging) must give `expected` for every entry of scale.next.
pattern: the slices, the checksums and the points of the slider track must match.
TABLE, TOKEN_TYPES and SLIDER_IDS must be frozen: an attempt to change them must throw or leave them as they are.

Why a tolerance: the JavaScript standard lets Math.pow differ in the last digits between browsers. Real differences are about 1e-15. This file was written with Node. Chrome and Safari agree with each other and differ from Node in the last digits of about one number in twenty.
hiddenWorkWarning: The hidden-work amounts in these vectors are placeholders. They are not researched values.
tipWarning: The shares in the example tips (half, 40%, 30%, all) are examples for testing only.

pattern.explanation: slices[dial].firstTwelve[run] is the slice (0 to 9999) that runs 0 to 11 use on that dial. checksum is the sum of (run + 1) × slice over all 10,000 runs. valueAt and positionOf hold points of the slider track. firstRuns holds the assumption values of runs 0 to 4.

vectors.why: Fixture A from the brief.

vectors.why: Fixture B from the brief.

vectors.name: C
vectors.title: Tiny

vectors.name: D

vectors.why: Fixture D from the brief. The energy high end is stretched.

vectors.name: zero-tokens
vectors.title: No tokens at all
vectors.why: Everything must be zero, with no "not a number" anywhere.

vectors.name: zero-counts
vectors.title: A model with zero tokens
vectors.why: The same as no tokens.

vectors.name: output-only
vectors.title: One token type: output
vectors.why: The three weights change nothing. The result is a plain product.

vectors.name: cache-read-only
vectors.title: One token type: cache reads
vectors.why: Only the cache-read weight, energy, overhead, grid and hardware matter.

vectors.name: one-token
vectors.title: A single output token
vectors.why: The smallest possible input: about 40 billionths of a kilogram.

vectors.name: huge
vectors.title: Fixture A times one million
vectors.why: Thousands of tonnes. Every result must be exactly one million times fixture A, give or take the last digit.

vectors.name: all-size-classes
vectors.title: All four size classes at once
vectors.why: The four energy values move together.

vectors.name: pinned-all-typical
vectors.title: Every slider set to typical
vectors.why: One outcome, no range. It equals the all-typical value of fixture A to the last digit.

vectors.name: pinned-all-low
vectors.title: Every slider set to low
vectors.why: One outcome. It equals the extreme low of fixture A.

vectors.name: pinned-all-high
vectors.title: Every slider set to high
vectors.why: One outcome. It equals the extreme high of fixture A.

vectors.name: pinned-energy-high
vectors.title: Energy slider set near high
vectors.why: A pinned slider can make the range wider in kg: 16 to 76 kg here, against 3.7 to 34 kg.

vectors.name: pinned-without-effect
vectors.title: A slider that changes nothing
vectors.why: Fixture B has no cache writes. Setting that slider gives exactly the numbers of fixture B. The slider is listed in `inert`.

vectors.name: almost-no-width
vectors.title: Every slider set but hardware
vectors.why: The likely range is only 1.9% wide: 8.50 to 8.65 kg. It is narrow, but it is not one outcome.

vectors.name: pins-as-values
vectors.title: Sliders handed over as values
vectors.why: A pin written { value } is the assumption's own value. The module turns it into a track position. For energy the value needs its model size.

vectors.name: single-is-about-the-runs
vectors.title: Almost every run gives the same number, but not all
vectors.why: A footprint so large that one more token is below what a number can hold. 9,888 of the 10,000 runs give the same number to the last digit. The other 112 do not. That is not "one outcome": `single` is about the lowest and the highest run, not about the two ends of the likely range.

vectors.name: hidden-work
vectors.title: ChatGPT with three pieces of hidden work
vectors.why: Placeholder amounts. Each amount is one more assumption with its own dial. The share of gpt-4o in `shares.models` includes its hidden work.

vectors.name: hidden-off-and-pinned
vectors.title: One piece switched off, one amount set by the person
vectors.why: The last piece is off. The first has its amount set.

vectors.name: hidden-first-off
vectors.title: The first piece switched off
vectors.why: Switching a piece off must not change which combinations the others use. The pieces after it keep their slots.

vectors.name: hidden-left-out
vectors.title: The first piece left out of the list
vectors.why: Every number equals the vector "hidden-first-off", except that a slider for the missing piece is not listed in `inert`. A piece that is left out counts as off, because the slot is given and not taken from the place in the list.

vectors.name: hidden-other-order
vectors.title: The same three pieces in another order
vectors.why: Every number equals the vector "hidden-work". The order of the list does not matter.

vectors.name: hidden-without-on
vectors.title: Three pieces that do not say whether they are on
vectors.why: A piece without `on` is counted. Every number equals the vector "hidden-work".

vectors.name: hidden-pin-for-off-piece
vectors.title: A set slider for a piece that is switched off
vectors.why: It is accepted and changes nothing. The numbers equal the vector "hidden-first-off".

vectors.name: hidden-six
vectors.title: Six pieces of hidden work, all on
vectors.why: All six slots of the pattern are in use, each with its own amount. One piece has cache writes. Two have rows for two models.

vectors.name: hidden-same-amount
vectors.title: Two pieces with the same low, typical and high
vectors.why: They still vary on their own, each on its own dial. They must not move together.

vectors.name: tips
vectors.title: Fixture A with two tips, none applied
vectors.why: Each saving range is worked out run by run.

vectors.title: Fixture A with the first tip applied
vectors.why: The shown range is the tip's "after" range. The baseline is the range of fixture A. `shares.models` still describes the usage as counted: Opus keeps its 82.5%.

tips.label: Half of the Opus tokens move to Sonnet
40% fewer cache-read tokens

vectors.name: tips-applied-with-pin
vectors.title: Both tips applied, one slider set
vectors.why: Tips, a pinned slider and the market-based alternative together.

tips.label: Half of the Opus tokens move to Sonnet
40% fewer cache-read tokens

vectors.name: while-dragging
vectors.title: What the page asks for while a slider is dragged
vectors.why: With { tips: false, biggestUnknown: false } the result has no tip entries and no biggest unknown. The baseline is still there.

tips.label: Half of the Opus tokens move to Sonnet
40% fewer cache-read tokens

vectors.name: tips-order
vectors.title: Two tips that do not commute, both applied
vectors.why: Applied tips are applied in the order of the tip list: first half of the medium tokens to a small model, then half of the small tokens to a medium one. The other order gives other numbers.

tips.label: Half of the medium tokens move to a small model
Half of the small tokens move to a medium model

vectors.name: tip-that-saves-nothing-half-the-time
vectors.title: All Fable tokens move to a large model
vectors.why: Fable and large models share their low and typical energy. So in 5,000 of the 10,000 runs the saving is exactly zero.

tips.label: All Fable tokens move to a large model

vectors.name: fable-and-opus
vectors.title: Fable and Opus, all Fable tokens move to a large model
vectors.why: With a second large model the two sums add up in another order. The saving in the 5,000 runs must still be exactly zero, not a rounding error below zero.

tips.label: All Fable tokens move to a large model

vectors.name: fable-part-moves
vectors.title: Fable, Sonnet and Haiku, 30% of the Fable tokens move
vectors.why: The same with a part of the tokens and two more model sizes. The smallest saving is exactly zero.

tips.label: 30% of the Fable tokens move to a large model

vectors.name: tip-capitals
vectors.title: A model name and a search text with capitals
vectors.why: modelIncludes ignores capitals on both sides.

tips.label: Half of the Opus tokens move to Sonnet

vectors.name: tip-exact-models
vectors.title: A tip that names its models exactly
vectors.why: where.models takes the exact names. A model whose name only contains the same text is left alone.

tips.label: Half of the Opus 5.5 tokens move to Sonnet

vectors.name: tip-row-already-there
vectors.title: Half of everything moves to a medium model
vectors.why: A row that is already in the target class is not split. So the shown usage has five rows, not six.

tips.label: Half of all tokens move to a medium model

vectors.name: tip-hidden-id
vectors.title: A tip on one piece of hidden work
vectors.why: scaleTokens with hiddenId changes the rows of that piece only, not the visible rows.

tips.label: Half as much hidden thinking

vectors.name: tip-moves-hidden
vectors.title: A model tip for ChatGPT, without and with the hidden work
vectors.why: The hidden work of a chat runs on the chat's model. With hidden: true it moves along, and the saving is about three times as large.

tips.label: Half of the GPT-4o tokens move to a small model, visible tokens only
The same, with the hidden work

vectors.name: tip-calls-estimate
vectors.title: A tip that calls estimate itself
vectors.why: Every tip runs before the first working array is filled. So the numbers equal those of the plain tip "clear" in the vector "tip-applied".

tips.label: Half of the Opus tokens move to Sonnet
40% fewer cache-read tokens, from a tip that looks at an estimate of its own first

vectors.name: market-based
vectors.title: Fixture A with market-based electricity
vectors.why: Electricity at 70 g per kWh. The hardware emissions stay the same in kg.

vectors.name: custom-table
vectors.title: A table with one more size class
vectors.why: Shows how a model that fits no class could be counted: a class "unknown" from the small low to the large high.

vectors.name: table-same-rows
vectors.title: A table whose fresh-input and cache-write rows are the same
vectors.why: The two weights still vary on their own. Two assumptions with the same low, typical and high must not move together.

vectors.name: table-other-typical
vectors.title: A table that differs in one typical value only
vectors.why: Grid 270 / 300 / 460 in place of 270 / 350 / 460. The module keeps value tables between calls. It must not hand this call the values of the default table. Run the vectors in one process, in the order of the file.
